name: Credgenics
tagline: Enterprise debt collections and recovery platform for banks, NBFCs and fintech lenders, covering digital outreach, field agents, legal workflows and payment collection.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Enterprise sales, no public list price.

verdictSummary: This is not an app, it is a regulated operations layer bolted onto a lender's loan book. The value sits in core banking and LMS integrations, telephony and SMS and WhatsApp delivery at millions of messages a month, field agent tracking, payment gateway reconciliation, and legal notice workflows that have to survive an audit and a regulator's collections code. An agent can absolutely build you a delinquency ledger with aging buckets and reminder sequences, and that is a genuinely useful weekend tool if you are chasing your own receivables. It cannot build the bank integrations, the licensed comms channels, the lawyer network, or the paper trail that makes a recovery action defensible. If you are actually collecting on consumer loans at scale, a personal build is not a replacement, it is a liability.
coreLoopDIY: A local ledger of who owes you what, with aging buckets, reminder sequences, promise-to-pay logging, and drafted follow-up emails you send yourself.
requirements: Node 20 and a local machine to run it on
Your own SMTP credentials in .env if you want reminders actually sent
A CSV export of whatever currently tracks your receivables
whatYouLose: Core banking and loan management system integrations, so nothing reconciles itself
Licensed telephony, IVR, SMS and WhatsApp delivery at scale, plus the consent and do-not-disturb plumbing around it
Field collections: agent apps, geotagged visits, receipt issuance, cash handling controls
Legal automation: notice generation, arbitration and Section 138 tracking, empanelled lawyer workflows
Audit trails and regulatory defensibility, which is the entire point when a collections practice gets questioned
moatNotes: Collections is one of the few software categories where the regulator, not the user, defines the feature list. Every recorded call and consent flag exists because someone can be fined for its absence.
whyPeopleStillPay: Lenders do not buy Credgenics because dunning emails are hard. They buy it because collections touches money movement, consumer protection rules, telephony licensing, field staff with cash in hand, and courts, all at once, and because a recovery rate improvement of a couple of percentage points on a large book pays for the contract many times over. Replacing that in-house means an integration project against your LMS, a comms vendor stack, a legal ops team, and an audit posture. The buyer is a collections head with a recovery target, not a person looking for a tidier spreadsheet.
notes: You can one-shot the nag-list, and the nag-list is genuinely the fun part. The moat is bank integrations plus a regulator watching every call recording, and no personal build gets to stand in front of that.
prompt:
Build a local-only receivables follow-up tracker called Dunner. This is a personal tool for chasing money people owe me, not a regulated collections platform.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/dunner.db, schema created on first boot.
- No auth, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud services. It runs on localhost.

Data model:
- debtor: name, email, phone, notes.
- account: debtor_id, reference, principal_amount, currency, due_date, status (current, overdue, promised, partial, settled, written_off).
- payment: account_id, amount, received_on, method, note.
- contact_log: account_id, channel (email, call, sms, in_person), direction, summary, occurred_at.
- promise: account_id, promised_amount, promised_date, kept (null until resolved).

Features, in scope:
- Dashboard with aging buckets: not yet due, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+ days past due. Show count and total outstanding per bucket.
- Account detail page: balance computed as principal minus payments, full contact log, promise history, one-click add payment.
- Reminder sequences: define named sequences as a list of steps (offset in days from due date, template name, tone label). Assign a sequence to an account. A "due today" queue lists which accounts need which step.
- Email templates as Markdown files in ./templates with {{name}}, {{amount}}, {{reference}}, {{days_overdue}} placeholders. Render a preview and a copy-to-clipboard button.
- Optional actual sending via nodemailer using SMTP_HOST, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS from .env. If those are absent, the send button is disabled and the app still works fully in copy-paste mode.
- CSV import for debtors and accounts, CSV export of everything.
- Broken-promise view: promises past their date with no matching payment.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build:
- SMS, WhatsApp, IVR, auto-dialers, or anything that needs a telecom vendor.
- Payment gateway collection or any money movement.
- Legal notice generation, court tracking, or lawyer assignment.
- Field agent apps, geotagging, multi-user roles.

Deliver a README with setup steps, a .env.example, seed data for five fake debtors, and one script npm run due that prints today's reminder queue to the terminal. Add a plain banner in the UI: this is a personal tracker and is not a compliant collections system.
